title: Home Purchase Financing — Assessing a Late Charge on an Installment
content:
**Servicing desk reference — late charges on Home Purchase Financing loans**

## When a late charge is owed

A late charge is owed on an installment that was not paid in full within its grace period, once the grace period has ended, whether the installment is still unpaid or was received late, and it is assessed against that installment. The installment charged is the oldest unpaid installment when its grace period has already ended, and otherwise the most recent installment received, received after its grace period.

A late charge, once assessed, is part of the fees owed on the loan.

| Situation of the installment once its grace period has ended | Late charge owed against it |
|---|---|
| still unpaid | yes |
| received after the grace period ended | yes |
| paid in full within the grace period | no |

## The system action: `assess_late_charge_8f52dfa4`

**Capability.** Assesses a late charge on a Hearthstone Home Finance loan for one installment, dated today. It books one late charge against the installment named by its due date and adds it to the fees the borrower owes on the loan; the charge then shows in the loan's transactions and in its fees balance. Nothing else on the loan changes.

**How it is invoked.** An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `assess_late_charge_8f52dfa4` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

- `loan_id` — the loan number of the Hearthstone Home Finance loan, as returned by the loan lookup for the verified borrower (identifier).
- `installment_due_date` — the due date of the installment the late charge is for, written YYYY-MM-DD.
- `amount` — the late charge in USD, a positive amount with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent.

**Return.** On success: `status` "assessed", `loan_txn_id` (reference of the late charge), `loan_id`, `installment_due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `txn_date` (today, YYYY-MM-DD), `amount` (USD, 2 decimal places) and `fees_balance` (USD, 2 decimal places, fees owed after the charge).
